subproblems.title: Graph coordinates on R^(n+l) and projection onto the rotated plane
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers n, l and every linear isometry equivalence q of R^(n+l) = EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)): (i) graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b') for all a, a' in R^n and b, b' in R^l; (ii) ||graphPoint a b||^2 = ||a||^2 + ||b||^2 for all a in R^n, b in R^l; (iii) every z in R^(n+l) equals graphPoint a b for some a in R^n and b in R^l; (iv) for all a in R^n and b in R^l, the orthogonal projection (starProjection) of R^(n+l) onto rotatedPlane q = q(horizontalPlane n l) maps q(graphPoint a b) to q(graphPoint a 0). Here graphPoint a b is the vector whose first n coordinates are a and whose last l coordinates are b.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ), (∀ (a a' : Rn n) (b b' : Rn ℓ), graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b')) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), ‖graphPoint a b‖ ^ 2 = ‖a‖ ^ 2 + ‖b‖ ^ 2) ∧ (∀ z : Amb n ℓ, ∃ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), z = graphPoint a b) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), (rotatedPlane q).starProjection (q (graphPoint a b)) = q (graphPoint a 0))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent's facts (G1) (subtraction form), (G2) and (G3), plus the projection identity that the sibling rotated_plane_dist uses in place of (G4). Exact reuse of the comparator-accepted declaration (candidate commit e2915745); the proof below is its accepted proof.

Notation. For a in R^n and b in R^l, graphPoint a b = toLp 2 (Fin.append (ofLp a) (ofLp b)) is the vector of R^(n+l) whose coordinate at index Fin.castAdd l i (i < n) is a_i and at index Fin.natAdd n j (j < l) is b_j (Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right). Every index k in Fin (n+l) has exactly one of these two forms (Fin.addCases). e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 is the k-th standard basis vector. H := horizontalPlane n l = span{e_(castAdd l i) : i < n}, T_0 := rotatedPlane q = q(H) (Submodule.map of q), and P is the orthogonal projection onto T_0 (starProjection).

1. (i) Both sides are vectors of R^(n+l); compare coordinates. Subtraction in EuclideanSpace is coordinatewise. At an index castAdd l i both sides equal a_i - a'_i, and at an index natAdd n j both sides equal b_j - b'_j (Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right). By Fin.addCases these are all indices, so graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b').
2. (ii) For z in EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)), |z|^2 = sum_k z_k^2 (EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq). Split the sum over Fin (n+l) into the castAdd part and the natAdd part (Fin.sum_univ_add). For z = graphPoint a b this gives sum_i a_i^2 + sum_j b_j^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2.
3. (iii) Given z, put a := (z_(castAdd l i))_(i<n) in R^n and b := (z_(natAdd n j))_(j<l) in R^l. By the coordinate description, graphPoint a b and z have the same coordinate at every index castAdd l i and natAdd n j, hence at every index, so z = graphPoint a b.
4. (iv) First, graphPoint a 0 = sum_i a_i e_(castAdd l i): at castAdd l i both sides equal a_i (castAdd is injective, so only the i-th summand contributes), and at natAdd n j both sides are 0 (natAdd n j differs from every castAdd l i', since n + j >= n > i'). So graphPoint a 0 is a linear combination of the generators of H, hence lies in H, and u := q(graphPoint a 0) lies in T_0 = q(H).
5. All castAdd-coordinates of graphPoint 0 b vanish, so <graphPoint 0 b, e_(castAdd l i)> = (graphPoint 0 b)_(castAdd l i) = 0 for every i. Hence every generator of H lies in the orthogonal complement of the line R(graphPoint 0 b), so H is contained in it (Submodule.span_le), i.e. <graphPoint 0 b, h> = 0 for every h in H.
6. A linear isometry preserves inner products (LinearIsometryEquiv.inner_map_map), so for every v = q(h) in T_0 (h in H) we get <q(graphPoint 0 b), v> = <graphPoint 0 b, h> = 0.
7. By (i), graphPoint a b - graphPoint a 0 = graphPoint (a - a) (b - 0) = graphPoint 0 b, and q is linear, so q(graphPoint a b) - u = q(graphPoint 0 b), which by step 6 is orthogonal to every element of T_0.
8. T_0 is finite dimensional, hence complete, and its orthogonal projection is characterized by: if u lies in T_0 and x - u is orthogonal to T_0, then P x = u (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero). With x = q(graphPoint a b) and u = q(graphPoint a 0), steps 4 and 7 give P(q(graphPoint a b)) = q(graphPoint a 0). This proves (iv).
proof_key_steps: Coordinatewise description of graphPoint via Fin.append and Fin.addCases
(i) subtraction is coordinatewise
(ii) split the Euclidean norm sum over Fin (n+l) with Fin.sum_univ_add
(iii) read off a and b from the castAdd and natAdd coordinates
(iv) graphPoint a 0 = sum_i a_i e_(castAdd l i) lies in the horizontal plane and graphPoint 0 b is orthogonal to it
q preserves inner products, so q(graphPoint a 0) lies in T_0 and q(graphPoint a b) - q(graphPoint a 0) = q(graphPoint 0 b) is orthogonal to T_0
eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero gives P(q(graphPoint a b)) = q(graphPoint a 0)

subproblems.title: graphPoint is the inverse of the canonical splitting of R^(n+l)
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers n, l and all x in R^n and y in R^l: graphPoint x y = E^(-1)(x, y), where E = EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : R^(n+l) ≃L[R] R^n x R^l is Mathlib's canonical continuous linear equivalence, which splits a vector of R^(n+l) into its first n and its last l coordinates.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (x : Rn n) (y : Rn ℓ), graphPoint x y = (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : Amb n ℓ ≃L[ℝ] Rn n × Rn ℓ).symm (x, y)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent's fact (G1) that graphPoint is linear in the pair (x, y), made precise by identifying graphPoint with the inverse of Mathlib's canonical equivalence; the sibling graph_plane_finrank uses it to see that v |-> q(graphPoint v (A v)) is an injective R-linear map. Exact reuse of the comparator-accepted declaration (candidate commit 18a457c4); the proof below is its accepted proof.

Fix n, l in N, x in R^n, y in R^l, let E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : R^(n+l) ≃L[R] R^n x R^l and w := E.symm (x, y).
1. (Coordinates of E.) By its definition (Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/PiL2.lean, section finAddEquivProd), E is the composite of the coordinate reindexing LinearIsometryEquiv.piLpCongrLeft 2 R R finSumFinEquiv.symm : EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)) -> EuclideanSpace R (Fin n ⊕ Fin l), which sends z to the vector b |-> z (finSumFinEquiv b), with EuclideanSpace.sumEquivProd, which splits a vector indexed by Fin n ⊕ Fin l into its Sum.inl-part and its Sum.inr-part. Since finSumFinEquiv (Sum.inl j) = Fin.castAdd l j and finSumFinEquiv (Sum.inr k) = Fin.natAdd n k (finSumFinEquiv_apply_left/right), for every z in R^(n+l) we get E z = ((z (Fin.castAdd l j))_(j : Fin n), (z (Fin.natAdd n k))_(k : Fin l)).
2. (Coordinates of w.) Since E is an equivalence, E w = E (E.symm (x, y)) = (x, y). Applying the formula of step 1 to z = w gives (w (Fin.castAdd l j))_j = x and (w (Fin.natAdd n k))_k = y, i.e. w (Fin.castAdd l j) = x_j for all j : Fin n and w (Fin.natAdd n k) = y_k for all k : Fin l.
3. (Coordinates of graphPoint x y.) By definition (graphPoint x y)(i) = Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y) i for all i : Fin (n+l), so (graphPoint x y)(Fin.castAdd l j) = x_j (Fin.append_left) and (graphPoint x y)(Fin.natAdd n k) = y_k (Fin.append_right).
4. (Conclusion.) Two vectors of EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)) are equal as soon as all their coordinates agree (ext), and every index i : Fin (n+l) is of the form Fin.castAdd l j with j : Fin n or Fin.natAdd n k with k : Fin l (Fin.addCases). By steps 2 and 3 the coordinates of graphPoint x y and of w agree in both cases. Hence graphPoint x y = w = E.symm (x, y). (Accepted Lean outline: ext i; refine Fin.addCases (fun j => ?_) (fun k => ?_) i, then simp [graphPoint] closes each case.)
proof_key_steps: E = finAddEquivProd (piLpCongrLeft finSumFinEquiv.symm followed by sumEquivProd) sends z to ((z (castAdd l j))_j, (z (natAdd n k))_k)
E w = (x, y) for w := E.symm (x, y), so w (castAdd l j) = x_j and w (natAdd n k) = y_k
Coordinates of graphPoint x y: castAdd l j |-> x_j, natAdd n k |-> y_k (Fin.append_left/right)
ext + Fin.addCases: all coordinates agree, so graphPoint x y = E.symm (x, y)

subproblems.title: Continuity and operator bounds for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers m, k: the map A |-> hsNormSq A on continuous linear maps R^m ->L[R] R^k is continuous (operator-norm topology), and every such A satisfies 0 <= hsNormSq A, hsNormSq A <= m ||A||^2 (||A|| the operator norm), and ||A v||^2 <= hsNormSq A ||v||^2 for all v in R^m. Here hsNormSq A = sum_(i<m) ||A e_i||^2 with e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ), Continuous (fun A : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k => hsNormSq A) ∧ ∀ A : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k, 0 ≤ hsNormSq A ∧ hsNormSq A ≤ m * ‖A‖ ^ 2 ∧ ∀ v : Rn m, ‖A v‖ ^ 2 ≤ hsNormSq A * ‖v‖ ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent's fact (G5), the operator bound |A a| <= |A| |a| proved by Cauchy-Schwarz; the parent uses the last conjunct together with 0 <= hsNormSq A. Exact reuse of the comparator-accepted declaration (candidate commit 7372f81c); the proof below is its accepted proof.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i in Fin m; these vectors form the standard orthonormal basis of R^m, so |e_i| = 1. For v in R^m, v_i denotes its i-th coordinate. By definition hsNormSq(A) = sum over i < m of |A e_i|^2. ||A|| is the operator norm of A : R^m ->L R^k.

1. Continuity. Fix i. The evaluation map A -> A e_i is linear in A and satisfies |A e_i - B e_i| = |(A - B) e_i| <= ||A - B|| |e_i| = ||A - B||, so it is continuous for the operator-norm topology. Composing with the continuous maps w -> |w| and t -> t^2 gives a continuous real function A -> |A e_i|^2. A finite sum of continuous real functions is continuous, so A -> sum_i |A e_i|^2 = hsNormSq(A) is continuous.
2. Nonnegativity. Every summand |A e_i|^2 is >= 0, hence hsNormSq(A) >= 0.
3. Upper bound by the operator norm. For each i, 0 <= |A e_i| <= ||A|| |e_i| = ||A||, so |A e_i|^2 <= ||A||^2. Summing over the m indices gives hsNormSq(A) <= sum_{i<m} ||A||^2 = m ||A||^2.
4. Coordinates. Every v in R^m satisfies v = sum_i v_i e_i, because the j-th coordinate of the right side is sum_i v_i delta_{ij} = v_j. For the Euclidean norm, |v|^2 = sum_i v_i^2 = sum_i |v_i|^2.
5. Bound on |A v|. By linearity of A and step 4, A v = sum_i v_i (A e_i). The triangle inequality and homogeneity of the norm give |A v| <= sum_i |v_i (A e_i)| = sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|.
6. Cauchy-Schwarz. For finite sums of real numbers, (sum_i a_i b_i)^2 <= (sum_i a_i^2)(sum_i b_i^2). With a_i = |v_i| and b_i = |A e_i| and step 4, (sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|)^2 <= (sum_i |v_i|^2)(sum_i |A e_i|^2) = |v|^2 hsNormSq(A).
7. Conclusion. Since 0 <= |A v| <= sum_i |v_i| |A e_i| (step 5), squaring preserves the inequality, and step 6 gives |A v|^2 <= (sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|)^2 <= hsNormSq(A) |v|^2. If m = 0, all sums are empty and v = 0, so each assertion reads 0 <= 0 and the steps above apply verbatim.

Lean notes (names that worked under the pinned toolchain): unfold hsNormSq, then fun_prop (step 1) and positivity (step 2); ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm and the norm of EuclideanSpace.single (step 3); ext with simp [Pi.single_apply] (step 4); map_sum, map_smul, norm_sum_le, norm_smul (step 5); Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq and EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq (step 6).
proof_key_steps: Continuity: each evaluation A -> A e_i is continuous linear, and hsNormSq is a finite sum of squared norms of such maps
Nonnegativity: hsNormSq A is a sum of squares
|A e_i| <= ||A|| |e_i| = ||A||; summing over i < m gives hsNormSq A <= m ||A||^2
Expand v = sum_i v_i e_i; linearity and the triangle inequality give |A v| <= sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|
Cauchy-Schwarz gives (sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|)^2 <= |v|^2 hsNormSq A; squaring the nonnegative bound gives |A v|^2 <= hsNormSq A |v|^2

subproblems.title: Dimension of a rotated linear graph plane
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers n, l, every linear isometry equivalence q of R^(n+l) and every continuous linear map A : R^n -> R^l, the subspace S = span_R{q(graphPoint v (A v)) : v in R^n} of R^(n+l) has dimension n, i.e. Module.finrank R S = n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => q (graphPoint v (A v)))) = n
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof, with the linearity of graphPoint supplied by the sibling graph_point_linear_equiv.

Fix n, l, q and A. Write S := span_R{q(graphPoint v (A v)) : v in R^n} and E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : R^(n+l) ≃L[R] R^n x R^l, Mathlib's canonical continuous linear equivalence.
1. (Representation.) By the sibling lemma rsod_graphPoint_eq_finAddEquivProd_symm, graphPoint x y = E.symm (x, y) for all x in R^n and y in R^l.
2. (A linear map.) Let Phi : R^n ->l[R] R^(n+l) be the composite of three R-linear maps: v |-> (v, A v) (LinearMap.prod of the identity and A), then E.symm : R^n x R^l -> R^(n+l), then q : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l). So Phi is R-linear, and by step 1, Phi v = q(E.symm (v, A v)) = q(graphPoint v (A v)) for every v in R^n.
3. (S is the range of Phi.) By step 2 the generating set {q(graphPoint v (A v)) : v in R^n} equals Set.range Phi. This is the carrier of the submodule LinearMap.range Phi (LinearMap.coe_range). The span of the carrier of a submodule is that submodule (Submodule.span_eq), so S = LinearMap.range Phi.
4. (Phi is injective.) Suppose Phi v = Phi w. By step 2, q(E.symm (v, A v)) = q(E.symm (w, A w)). The linear isometry equivalence q is injective, and so is the equivalence E.symm. Hence (v, A v) = (w, A w) in R^n x R^l, and comparing first components gives v = w. This is the parent's observation that graphPoint v (A v) determines v, because its first n coordinates are v.
5. (Dimension count.) An injective linear map has range of the same finrank as its domain (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj). By steps 3 and 4, finrank S = finrank (LinearMap.range Phi) = finrank R^n. Since R^n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) has finrank n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), finrank S = n.

    intro v w hvw
    rw [hΦ, hΦ, rsod_graphPoint_eq_finAddEquivProd_symm,
      rsod_graphPoint_eq_finAddEquivProd_symm] at hvw

    exact (Prod.mk.inj h).1

subproblems.title: Distance from a graph point to the rotated coordinate plane
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers n, l, every linear isometry equivalence q of R^(n+l), every a in R^n and every b in R^l, the distance from q(graphPoint a b) to the rotated plane rotatedPlane q = q(horizontalPlane n l), regarded as a set, equals ||b||: infDist (q(graphPoint a b)) (rotatedPlane q) = ||b||.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), infDist (q (graphPoint a b)) (rotatedPlane q : Set (Amb n ℓ)) = ‖b‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5(a) of the parent proof, strengthened to an equality. The facts (G1)-(G3) and the projection identity that replaces (G4) come from the sibling graph_coordinates.

Fix n, l, q, a, b. Write P := rotatedPlane q = q(horizontalPlane n l), a submodule of R^(n+l) regarded as a set in infDist. Let pi := P.starProjection be the orthogonal projection onto P, which exists because P is finite dimensional. By the sibling lemma lip_approx_graph_coordinates applied to n, l, q, for all c, c' in R^n and d, d' in R^l:
(G1) graphPoint c d - graphPoint c' d' = graphPoint (c - c') (d - d');
(G2) ||graphPoint c d||^2 = ||c||^2 + ||d||^2;
(G3) every z in R^(n+l) equals graphPoint c d for some c, d;
(P) pi(q(graphPoint c d)) = q(graphPoint c 0).
1. (Norm consequences of (G2).) For all c, d: ||d|| <= ||graphPoint c d||, because ||graphPoint c d||^2 = ||c||^2 + ||d||^2 >= ||d||^2 and both norms are nonnegative. Also ||graphPoint 0 d|| = ||d||, because ||graphPoint 0 d||^2 = 0 + ||d||^2 and both norms are nonnegative.
2. (Points q(graphPoint c 0) lie in P.) For c in R^n, (P) with d = 0 gives q(graphPoint c 0) = pi(q(graphPoint c 0)). The projection pi takes values in P (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem), so q(graphPoint c 0) lies in P.
3. (Every point of P has this form.) Let p in P. By (G3) applied to q^(-1)(p), there are c, d with q^(-1)(p) = graphPoint c d, so p = q(graphPoint c d). Since p lies in P, pi p = p (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff). By (P), pi p = q(graphPoint c 0). Hence p = q(graphPoint c 0).
4. (Upper bound.) By step 2 with c = a, the point q(graphPoint a 0) lies in P, so infDist(q(graphPoint a b), P) <= dist(q(graphPoint a b), q(graphPoint a 0)) (infDist_le_dist_of_mem). This distance equals ||q(graphPoint a b) - q(graphPoint a 0)||, which is ||q(graphPoint a b - graphPoint a 0)|| since q is linear, and then ||graphPoint a b - graphPoint a 0|| since q is an isometry. By (G1) this is ||graphPoint (a - a) (b - 0)|| = ||graphPoint 0 b||, which is ||b|| by step 1. So infDist(q(graphPoint a b), P) <= ||b||.
5. (Lower bound.) P is nonempty since 0 lies in P. For a nonempty set s, r <= infDist(x, s) holds iff r <= dist(x, y) for all y in s (Metric.le_infDist). So let p in P. By step 3, p = q(graphPoint c 0) for some c. Then dist(q(graphPoint a b), p) = ||q(graphPoint a b - graphPoint c 0)|| = ||graphPoint a b - graphPoint c 0|| = ||graphPoint (a - c) (b - 0)|| = ||graphPoint (a - c) b||, using the linearity and isometry of q and (G1). By step 1 this is >= ||b||. Hence ||b|| <= infDist(q(graphPoint a b), P).
6. Steps 4 and 5 give infDist(q(graphPoint a b), rotatedPlane q) = ||b||.

The only other declaration in scope was a stub of the sibling lip_approx_graph_coordinates. #print axioms gave [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
  intro n ℓ q a b
  obtain ⟨hsub, hnorm, hsurj, hproj⟩ := lip_approx_graph_coordinates n ℓ q
  -- `‖graphPoint 0 d‖ = ‖d‖` and `‖d‖ ≤ ‖graphPoint c d‖`
  have hge : ∀ (c : Rn n) (d : Rn ℓ), ‖d‖ ≤ ‖graphPoint c d‖ := by
    intro c d
    have h := hnorm c d
    have h0 : 0 ≤ ‖graphPoint c d‖ := norm_nonneg _
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg ‖c‖, norm_nonneg d]
  have hzero : ∀ d : Rn ℓ, ‖graphPoint (0 : Rn n) d‖ = ‖d‖ := by
    intro d
    have h := hnorm 0 d
    rw [norm_zero, zero_pow two_ne_zero, zero_add] at h
    exact (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mp h
  -- every point `q (graphPoint c 0)` lies in `T₀ = rotatedPlane q`
  have hmem : ∀ c : Rn n, q (graphPoint c 0) ∈ rotatedPlane q := by
    intro c
    rw [← hproj c 0]
    exact Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem _ _
  -- every point of `T₀` is of the form `q (graphPoint c 0)`
  have hform : ∀ p ∈ rotatedPlane q, ∃ c : Rn n, p = q (graphPoint c 0) := by
    intro p hp
    obtain ⟨c, d, hcd⟩ := hsurj (q.symm p)
    have hp' : p = q (graphPoint c d) := by
      rw [← hcd]
      simp
    refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
    have h := hproj c d
    rw [← hp', Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff.mpr hp] at h
    exact h
  apply le_antisymm
  · calc infDist (q (graphPoint a b)) (rotatedPlane q : Set (Amb n ℓ))
        ≤ dist (q (graphPoint a b)) (q (graphPoint a 0)) := infDist_le_dist_of_mem (hmem a)
      _ = ‖b‖ := by
        rw [dist_eq_norm, ← map_sub, LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map, hsub, sub_self, sub_zero,
          hzero]
  · rw [le_infDist ⟨0, (rotatedPlane q).zero_mem⟩]
    intro p hp
    obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hform p hp
    rw [dist_eq_norm, ← map_sub, LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map, hsub, sub_zero]
    exact hge _ _

q(graphPoint c 0) = pi(q(graphPoint c 0)) lies in P = rotatedPlane q
Every p in P equals q(graphPoint c 0): apply (G3) to q^(-1) p and use pi p = p together with (P)
Upper bound: infDist <= dist to q(graphPoint a 0) = ||graphPoint 0 b|| = ||b||
Lower bound via le_infDist: dist to q(graphPoint c 0) is ||graphPoint (a - c) b||, which is >= ||b||
